matched_direct_reference.interpretation: The observed deficit is approximately 15-16x on the matched panel-native direct target.

wsi_profile.interpretation: Virtual WSI is below 2 ms per present at the client boundary and is not the 500 ms frame-time bottleneck. The earlier E116 Activity copy/present sample was 2.990 ms per frame and is corroborative rather than part of this run's totals.

live_system_profile.interpretation: Android confines the Termux-owned game and Bionic service to the four efficiency cores while the separate visible Activity is top-app. This is a real secondary CPU defect, but it cannot explain the measured hundreds of milliseconds of synchronous bridge waits by itself.

diagnosis.evidence: The benchmark scene averages about 530 synchronous descriptor allocations and 529 synchronous update-template calls per present; the peak window exceeds 1,000 of each and spends 306.6 ms per 500 ms frame in those two calls alone.

diagnosis.cause: synchronous queue submission and semaphore waits
diagnosis.evidence: Heavy windows spend about 115.1 ms per present in opcodes 105, 83, and 85.

diagnosis.cause: Android background/moderate scheduling on efficiency cores
diagnosis.evidence: Both game and service are restricted to CPUs 0-3 while CPUs 4-7 are faster and the Activity is top-app.

diagnosis.cause: remaining game/FEX/DXVK CPU work and possible GPU work
diagnosis.evidence: The measured bridge RPC budget does not cover the entire 500 ms frame. KGSL busy counters were unavailable, so this run does not assign the remainder to the GPU.

rejected_primary_causes: PRoot in the game Vulkan path
current memory pressure or storage page-in during the sample
recommended_order: E126: move vkUpdateDescriptorSetWithTemplate payloads into a bounded shared descriptor journal and replay them in sequence at the existing submit boundary, removing hundreds to thousands of socket round trips per frame
E127: replace per-set synchronous allocation with a bounded descriptor arena/lease protocol or shared request-completion ring; preserve descriptor-pool reset epochs and fail closed on exhaustion
E128: move QueueSubmit2 and semaphore completion traffic to a shared submission/completion ring while retaining native Bionic synchronization semantics
E129: launch the game/service from an Activity-owned foreground execution path or equivalent broker so the hot threads can use CPUs 4-7; isolate the busy RakNet thread from dxvk-cs
After the CPU/IPC gates, capture real Turnip GPU timestamps or Perfetto/KGSL counters before changing graphics work

expected_near_term_ceiling.statement: Removing descriptor RPC time alone would reduce the measured heavy-scene blocking budget from about 307 ms to about 127 ms, but it does not guarantee the final frame time because CPU, submission, and GPU work can overlap or move.
expected_near_term_ceiling.honest_target_after_descriptor_and_submi: first recover into the high single digits, then measure; 20-30 FPS remains possible but is not yet supported by BVB data

reuse: The required deja queries for this exact completed-game descriptor storm returned no indexed implementation. The profile reuses E116's bounded 32-present WSI timing, E117's bounded per-opcode RPC histogram, and E124's first complete benchmark boundary; no invasive per-call logging was added for this run.
